pass_a_gloss: [...] But, O you having a vain brow over nothing, did you not hear these things long ago, which I did? For if indeed you should wish, he says, to look closely into the words of my prophets, I said already beforehand that these things will happen. For I from ancient days arranged, that is, I determined and assented; and now, the time calling, I showed forth to an end the things announced, so as to lay waste nations in strong cities, that is, not weak and easily taken. I let go the hands, and they were dried up. For I who of old was still holding them together by forbearances toward being, and standing together, removed the defending hand, and like grass they dried up, and like hay they withered, and as some dry couch grass they have been given as food to fire. This indeed he says to him elsewhere too; for since the ungodly one, having accomplished the things determined to happen by God, thought great of himself, he was hearing God saying again: Will an axe be glorified without the one cutting with it? Or will a saw be lifted up without the one drawing it? For just as such of the tools do not move themselves to works, but rather wait for the hand of the one shaking them, thus you too, he says, have become a tool of the divine wrath, not that you yourself worked by your own powers, but you were rather as an axe and saw appointed to serve the wills of the one moving. [Lemma, Isaiah 37:28-29:] But now your rest and your going out I know; and your wrath with which you were enraged, and your bitterness went up to me. You boast then, he says, having become a servant of the divine judgments, and you think perhaps that by yourself and alone you prevailed over so many nations and countries, so as to burn and take them. But I know your rest, and the going out and the coming in. And rest, as I think, he names death, and going out and coming in the way into anything whatever of the things to be done. For nothing at all escapes the mind that knows all. And adding that, Your wrath with which you were enraged and your bitterness went up to me, he all but says: Not without penalty will you have blasphemed. For I will in no way overlook the malice and bitterness of your unholy thoughts, but as one provoked to grief I will lay upon your rages the penalty fitting them. [Lemma, Isaiah 37:29:] And I will put a muzzle into your nose, and a bridle into your lips, and I will turn you back by the road in which you were coming. Since the Assyrian, having a senselessness most befitting cattle, was mocking God, and as having leapt into unbridled wildness he was letting loose voices of ill speech against the glory of God, for this reason indeed very fittingly as upon a beast he says that, I will put a muzzle into your nose, and a bridle into your lips, all but by the bringings-on of blows [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …? But you, who lift your brows in vain over nothing, “have you not heard long ago these things which I have done?” (Isaiah 37:26). For if only you were willing, He says, to look closely into the words of My prophets, I said beforehand that these things would come to pass. For “I arranged them from ancient days” (Isaiah 37:26), that is, I decreed them and gave My assent; and now, when the time called for it, I have brought what was foretold to its end, so as “to lay waste nations in strong cities” (Isaiah 37:26), that is, cities that were not weak or easily taken.

“I let go My hands, and they were dried up” (Isaiah 37:27). For I, who long held them together through My forbearance so that they might exist and stand, withdrew the hand that defended them; and they withered like grass, faded like hay, and, like dry couch grass, were given as food to the fire.

This is what He says to him in another place too. For when the ungodly man had carried out what God had decreed should happen and thought great things of himself, he heard God saying again: “Shall the axe be glorified without the one who cuts with it? Or shall the saw be exalted without the one who draws it?” (Isaiah 10:15). For just as such tools do not, of course, move themselves to their work, but rather wait for the hand that moves them, so you too, He says, have become an instrument of the divine wrath. You did not do these things by your own powers; rather, you were like an axe and a saw, appointed to serve the will of the one who moves you.
“But now I know your rest and your going out; and your wrath with which you raged, and your bitterness, has come up to Me” (Isaiah 37:28-29).

So you boast, He says, though you were only the servant of the divine judgments, and perhaps you think that by yourself and alone you prevailed over so many nations and lands, so as to burn them and take them. But I know your rest, your going out and your coming in. By rest, as I think, He means death; and by going out and coming in, the path into anything whatever that is to be done. For nothing at all escapes the Mind that knows all things.

And when He adds, “Your wrath with which you raged, and your bitterness, has come up to Me,” He all but says: You will not have blasphemed without punishment. For I will by no means overlook the malice and bitterness of your unholy thoughts; but, as one provoked to grief, I will lay on your rages the penalty that befits them.
“And I will put a muzzle in your nose and a bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you were coming” (Isaiah 37:29).

Since the Assyrian, in a senselessness most like a beast's, mocked God, and, as though he had bolted into unbridled wildness, let loose words of blasphemy against the glory of God, for this reason He says, and very fittingly, as of a beast: “I will put a muzzle in your nose and a bridle in your lips,” all but saying that by the blows He would bring upon him …

choices.english: You will not have blasphemed without punishment
choices.why: The double negative makes a plain threat of penalty.

choices.english: the Mind that knows all things
choices.why: God named as the all-knowing Mind; capitalised because it means God.
